check.hostEmpty: Please enter a host, e.g. git.company.example or git.company.example:8443.

title: Network
intro: Proxy and certificates for this app's connections to HTTP(S) remotes. Your own Git configuration stays untouched; SSH connections are not affected.
warning_one: Certificate verification is turned off for {{count}} host
warning_other: Certificate verification is turned off for {{count}} hosts
warningBody: On these connections, anyone on the network can pose as the server, read credentials and alter code. You can turn it back on per host below.

proxy.title: Proxy
proxy.description: All HTTP(S) remotes go through this proxy, e.g. http://proxy.company.example:8080 – also https, socks4 and socks5. Empty: direct connection.

perHost.title: Proxy per host
perHost.intro: Use a different proxy for individual servers – or none, e.g. for the Git server on your own network.
perHost.empty: No exceptions: the proxy above applies to every host.
perHost.proxy: Proxy for this host (empty = no proxy)

caBundle.title: Custom CA bundle
caBundle.description: PEM file with the certificates Git trusts instead of the system list – e.g. your server's self-signed certificate or your company's certificate authority. Empty: the system certificates.

noVerify.title: Turn off certificate verification per host
noVerify.intro: Only as a last resort, if a server's certificate cannot be added as a CA bundle. Verification is then skipped for exactly this host – never for all.
noVerify.empty: The certificate is verified for every host.
noVerify.confirmBody: The app then no longer checks whether this server is really at the other end. Anyone listening on the same network can capture credentials and slip you altered code. It is safer to add the server's certificate as a CA bundle above. The exception only applies to this host and can be undone here at any time.
